title: XSS Prevention
definition: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS): A vulnerability where an attacker injects malicious JavaScript into a website, which then executes in the browser of other users.
simpleExplanation: An attacker writes `<script>stealPasswords()</script>` in a blog comment. If your website blindly renders that comment, the browser will execute the script. React and Next.js automatically prevent this by 'escaping' all text.
realWorldExample: A forum website. You must ensure that if someone pastes JavaScript into a forum post, it displays as raw text on the screen, rather than actually running the code.

basic:
Does React automatically protect you from XSS attacks when rendering variables like `
{userData}
`?
intermediate: What specific React property explicitly bypasses this protection and leaves you vulnerable to XSS?

answers.question: Automatically protect?
answers.answer: Yes. React automatically sanitizes (escapes) all variables placed in curly braces before rendering them to the DOM.

answers.question: Which property bypasses?
answers.answer: `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. If you use this, you MUST manually sanitize the input using a library like DOMPurify.
